name: Aloo Paratha
description: Crispy whole wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potato.
steps: Boil and mash potatoes. Mix with onion, chilli, coriander, salt.
Knead atta into smooth dough.
Stuff and roll flat.
Cook on hot tawa with ghee until golden.
Serve hot with curd and pickle.

name: Dal Tadka
description: Comforting lentil curry with a sizzling spiced tadka.
steps: Pressure cook dal with turmeric and salt.
Saute onion, ginger-garlic, tomato and spices.
Add cooked dal and simmer 10 mins.
Pour cumin-chilli tadka.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
description: Silky, rich tomato-based gravy with soft paneer cubes.
steps: Blend tomato, onion, cashew, ginger, garlic into paste.
Cook paste in butter, add spices.
Add paneer and simmer 10 mins.
Finish with cream and sugar.

name: Poha
description: Light and fluffy flattened rice breakfast tossed with spices.
steps: Rinse poha and let soften 5 mins.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli in oil.
Add onion and cook.
Mix in poha, turmeric, salt, sugar.
Squeeze lemon and serve.

name: Rajma Chawal
description: Classic kidney bean curry served over steamed rice - ultimate comfort food.
steps: Soak rajma overnight, pressure cook.
Saute onion, ginger-garlic.
Add tomato and spices, cook until oil separates.
Add rajma and simmer 20 min.
Serve with steamed rice.

name: Masala Chai
description: Aromatic spiced Indian tea brewed to perfection.
steps: Boil water with ginger and cardamom.
Add tea leaves and simmer 2 mins.
Add milk and sugar.
Strain and serve hot.

name: Besan Chilla
description: Protein-rich gram flour pancakes - quick, crispy and delicious.
steps: Mix besan with water into smooth batter.
Add veggies and spices.
Pour on hot pan and spread thin.
Cook both sides until golden brown.

name: Palak Paneer
description: Creamy spinach gravy with golden paneer cubes - rich, vibrant and nutritious.
steps: Blanch spinach and blend smooth.
Saute onion, ginger-garlic.
Add spices and spinach puree.
Add paneer and simmer.
Finish with cream.

name: Chole Bhature
description: Spicy chickpea curry served with fluffy deep-fried bread - a North Indian favourite.
steps: Soak and pressure cook chole.
Saute onion, ginger-garlic.
Add tomato and masala, cook until oil separates.
Add chole and simmer.
Knead maida dough, roll and deep fry bhature.

name: Chicken Biryani
description: Aromatic layered rice and chicken cooked dum-style for a regal feast.
steps: Marinate chicken with curd and spices 30 min.
Parboil rice with whole spices.
Fry onions until caramelised.
Layer chicken and rice in pot.
Dum cook on low flame 25 min.

name: Masala Dosa
description: Crispy fermented rice crepe filled with spiced potato - South India's signature dish.
steps: Soak and grind rice+dal, ferment overnight.
Prepare potato masala filling.
Spread thin batter on hot tawa.
Add filling, fold and serve with sambar.

name: Egg Bhurji
description: Spicy Indian scrambled eggs with onion, tomato and green chilli.
steps: Beat eggs lightly.
Saute onion, chilli, tomato.
Add eggs and scramble on medium heat.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
description: Wholesome one-pot lentil and rice comfort food, perfect for any time of day.
steps: Rinse dal and rice.
Pressure cook with turmeric, salt and water.
Temper with ghee, cumin, ginger.
Mix and serve hot.

name: Aloo Gobi
description: Dry spiced potato and cauliflower stir-fry - a North Indian classic.
steps: Cut potato and cauliflower into florets.
Temper cumin in oil.
Add veggies and spices.
Cook covered until tender.
Serve with roti.

name: Sweet Lassi
description: Creamy, frothy chilled yogurt drink — Punjab's most beloved cooling refreshment.
steps: Add curd, milk and sugar to a blender.
Blend on high for 1 minute until frothy.
Add cardamom and rose water if using.
Pour into tall glasses over ice and serve chilled.

name: Mango Lassi
description: Thick, golden mango lassi — sweet, tropical and utterly refreshing.
steps: Peel and chop the mango, remove the seed.
Blend mango, curd, milk and sugar until silky smooth.
Add cardamom and blend briefly.
Serve chilled, garnished with saffron strands.

name: Nimbu Pani
description: India's classic street-side lemonade — tangy, sweet and instantly cooling.
steps: Squeeze lemon juice into a glass.
Add sugar and a pinch of salt, stir well.
Fill with cold water and ice cubes.
Add black salt and mint for the street-side touch.

name: Masala Chaas
description: Spiced thin buttermilk — the perfect digestive after a heavy Indian meal.
steps: Blend curd with water to thin consistency.
Add ginger, green chilli, cumin and blend again.
Season with salt and black salt.
Pour over ice, garnish with mint and coriander, serve cold.

name: Haldi Doodh
description: Golden turmeric milk — an ancient Ayurvedic remedy that warms you from within.
steps: Heat milk in a saucepan on medium flame.
Whisk in turmeric, pepper and ginger.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes without boiling.
Remove from heat, stir in honey and cardamom. Serve warm.

name: Cold Coffee
description: Thick, frothy blended cold coffee — a café favourite made right at home.
steps: Dissolve instant coffee and sugar in 2 tbsp warm water.
Add cold milk, cream and ice cubes to a blender.
Pour in the coffee mixture.
Blend until frothy. Serve immediately.

name: Badam Milk
description: Richly flavoured almond milk with saffron and cardamom — luxurious and nourishing.
steps: Soak almonds in water for 30 min, peel and blend with 1/4 cup milk.
Warm remaining milk in a pan.
Add almond paste, sugar and cardamom, simmer 5 min.
Add saffron dissolved in warm milk. Serve hot or cold.

name: Rose Milk
description: Delicate pink rose-flavoured milk — elegant, floral and refreshingly sweet.
steps: Chill the milk thoroughly.
Mix in rose water and sugar, stir until dissolved.
Add a few strands of saffron for colour.
Serve over ice in a tall glass.

name: Thandai
description: Festive chilled spiced milk drink with nuts and aromatic spices — Holi's signature drink.
steps: Soak almonds, cashews and fennel seeds for 2 hours.
Blend soaked ingredients with cardamom and pepper into a fine paste.
Add paste to chilled milk with sugar and rose water, stir well.
Strain through a muslin cloth. Serve cold with ice.

name: Aam Panna
description: Tangy raw mango cooler with mint and spices — the ultimate Indian summer drink.
steps: Boil or roast the raw mango until soft. Peel and extract pulp.
Blend pulp with mint, sugar, cumin and salts.
Dilute with cold water to taste.
Serve over ice with a mint sprig.

name: Jaljeera
description: Zesty cumin-mint water with black salt — India's ultimate digestive cooler.
steps: Dry roast cumin and grind coarsely.
Blend mint, coriander and ginger with a splash of water.
Mix lemon juice, cumin powder, mint paste and black salt.
Dilute with cold water, strain and serve over ice.

name: Shikanji
description: Classic North Indian spiced lemonade with ginger and cumin — tangy and energising.
steps: Squeeze lemon juice into a glass.
Grate ginger and extract juice from it.
Mix lemon juice, ginger juice, sugar, cumin and black salt.
Add cold water and ice, stir well. Garnish with mint.

name: Butter Chicken
description: Velvety tomato-cream gravy hugging tender chicken — the dish that made Indian food famous worldwide.
steps: Marinate chicken in curd and spices 30 min.
Blend tomato, garlic, ginger, cashew into sauce.
Cook sauce in butter, add chicken.
Finish with cream and simmer 10 min.

name: Aloo Tikki
description: Crispy spiced potato patties — North India's favourite street snack.
steps: Boil and mash potatoes.
Mix with spices, chilli and coriander.
Shape into flat patties, coat with besan.
Shallow fry until golden and crispy on both sides.

name: Matar Paneer
description: Soft paneer and sweet green peas in a rich spiced tomato gravy.
steps: Saute cumin, onion, ginger-garlic.
Add tomato and spices, cook until masala forms.
Add peas and paneer, simmer 10 min.
Finish with cream, garnish with coriander.

name: Dal Makhani
description: Slow-cooked black lentils in buttery tomato gravy — a Punjabi restaurant classic.
steps: Soak whole urad dal and rajma overnight, pressure cook.
Saute onion, ginger-garlic, tomato in butter.
Add cooked dal, simmer 30 min on low.
Finish with cream and butter.

name: Kadai Paneer
description: Smoky paneer and capsicum cooked with aromatic kadai masala in a wok.
steps: Dry roast coriander and red chilli, coarsely grind.
Saute onion, capsicum until slightly charred.
Add ginger-garlic, tomato and ground spices.
Add paneer, toss on high heat. Garnish with coriander.

name: Aloo Matar
description: Simple, homely potato and pea curry — everyday comfort food at its finest.
steps: Temper cumin in oil.
Add onion, cook till golden. Add tomato and spices.
Add potato cubes and peas.
Cook covered until potatoes are tender. Garnish.

name: Baingan Bharta
description: Smoky fire-roasted eggplant mash tempered with spiced onion-tomato masala.
steps: Roast brinjal directly on flame until charred and soft.
Peel, discard skin and mash the pulp.
Saute onion, ginger-garlic, tomato and spices.
Fold in mashed brinjal. Garnish with coriander.

name: Sarson Da Saag
description: Slow-cooked Punjab mustard greens with a dollop of white butter — winter perfection.
steps: Blanch mustard greens and spinach in salted water.
Blend coarsely, cook with maida to thicken.
Prepare tempering with onion, ginger-garlic, green chilli.
Mix tempering into saag. Top with makhan (butter).

name: Pindi Chole
description: Robust dry-style Rawalpindi chickpea curry with whole spices — deeply flavourful.
steps: Soak and pressure cook chickpeas with bay leaf and salt.
Saute onion until dark brown.
Add ginger-garlic, tomato and masalas.
Add chickpeas, cook until gravy is thick and coats the chana.

name: Gajar Ka Halwa
description: Slow-cooked grated carrot pudding with khoya and nuts — the queen of Indian desserts.
steps: Grate carrots. Cook in ghee on medium heat 5 min.
Add milk and simmer until fully absorbed.
Add sugar, cook until halwa leaves sides of pan.
Add cardamom and garnish with fried nuts.

name: Samosa
description: Crispy golden pastry stuffed with spiced potato-pea filling — India's iconic snack.
steps: Make stiff dough with maida, oil and water.
Prepare potato-pea filling with spices.
Roll, shape into cones, fill and seal samosas.
Deep fry on medium heat until golden and crispy.

name: Mutton Curry
description: Slow-cooked bone-in mutton in a deep, spicy onion-tomato gravy with aromatic spices.
steps: Marinate mutton in curd and spices for 1 hour.
Brown onions deeply. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato and masala, cook until oil separates.
Add mutton and pressure cook 30 min. Finish on open flame.

name: Paneer Tikka
description: Smoky, charred paneer and veggie skewers — the vegetarian equivalent of tandoori magic.
steps: Mix curd with spices for marinade.
Cube paneer, capsicum and onion, coat in marinade.
Skewer and grill or cook in a hot pan.
Squeeze lemon and serve with mint chutney.

name: Dum Aloo
description: Baby potatoes slow-cooked in a bold, aromatic yogurt-based gravy — a Kashmiri treasure.
steps: Deep fry parboiled baby potatoes until golden.
Blend onion, tomato and spices into gravy.
Cook gravy until oil separates. Add fried potatoes.
Seal with lid (dum) and cook on low 15 min.

name: Dal Khichdi
description: The Indian soul food — mixed dal and rice cooked into a nourishing one-pot meal.
steps: Rinse rice and dals together.
Pressure cook with turmeric, salt and water (5 whistles).
Temper cumin and ginger in ghee.
Mix tempering into khichdi. Serve with ghee and pickle.

name: Idli
description: Soft, pillowy steamed rice cakes — South India's most beloved and nutritious breakfast.
steps: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 6 hours.
Grind into smooth batter, ferment overnight.
Season with salt, pour into idli moulds.
Steam for 10-12 minutes. Serve with sambar and chutney.

name: Sambar
description: Tangy, spiced lentil-vegetable stew — the soul of South Indian cuisine.
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric.
Boil tamarind water with vegetables 10 min.
Add cooked dal and sambar powder, simmer 15 min.
Finish with mustard-curry leaf tempering.

name: Medu Vada
description: Crispy, fluffy deep-fried lentil donuts with a spiced crust — served with sambar and chutney.
steps: Soak urad dal 4 hours, grind into thick fluffy batter.
Add ginger, chilli, curry leaves and salt.
Shape into rings with a hole (like donuts).
Deep fry on medium heat until golden brown.

name: Rava Upma
description: Savoury semolina porridge with curry leaves and mustard — quick and wholesome.
steps: Dry roast rava until aromatic, set aside.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, peanuts in oil.
Saute onion, ginger and chilli.
Add hot water and rava, stir quickly. Cook covered 5 min.

name: Coconut Chutney
description: Creamy coconut chutney with ginger and a mustard-curry leaf tempering — the idli's best friend.
steps: Blend coconut, green chilli, ginger with water into smooth paste.
Add salt and lemon juice, blend again.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Pour tempering over chutney. Serve with idli/dosa.

name: Dhokla
description: Light, spongy steamed gram flour cake with a sweet-sour tempering — Gujarat's pride.
steps: Mix besan with curd, water, lemon juice and salt. Rest 20 min.
Add eno/baking soda, pour into greased plate.
Steam for 15 minutes. Cool and cut into squares.
Pour mustard-curry leaf tempering over dhokla.

name: Thepla
description: Thin spiced flatbread with fresh fenugreek leaves — Gujarat's go-to travel snack.
steps: Mix all ingredients into soft dough using water.
Roll into thin circles.
Cook on hot tawa with light oil on both sides.
Serve with pickle or curd.

name: Pav Bhaji
description: Buttery spiced mixed vegetable mash served with toasted bread rolls — Mumbai's street icon.
steps: Boil and mash all vegetables together.
Cook onion-tomato masala in butter.
Add mashed vegetables and pav bhaji masala.
Simmer until thick. Serve with butter-toasted pav.

name: Misal Pav
description: Spicy sprouted lentil curry topped with farsan — Maharashtra's spiciest and most iconic dish.
steps: Sprout moong overnight. Pressure cook lightly.
Make masala with onion, tomato, coconut, garlic.
Cook sprouted moong in spicy masala.
Serve as usal topped with farsan, onion and lemon.

name: Kheer
description: Slow-simmered creamy rice pudding with cardamom and saffron — India's timeless dessert.
steps: Wash rice. Bring milk to boil in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Add rice, simmer on low stirring frequently for 40 min.
Add sugar, cardamom and saffron.
Garnish with nuts. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Gulab Jamun
description: Soft, melt-in-mouth milk dumplings soaked in fragrant rose-cardamom syrup.
steps: Mix khoya with maida into soft dough. Shape into smooth balls.
Make sugar syrup with cardamom, rose water and saffron.
Deep fry gulab jamuns on very low heat until dark brown.
Soak in warm sugar syrup for 30 min.

name: Jalebi
description: Crispy orange swirls soaked in saffron syrup — India's most nostalgic sweet.
steps: Make thin batter with maida, curd and water. Ferment 4 hours.
Prepare one-string sugar syrup with cardamom and saffron.
Pipe batter in spiral through a piped bag into hot oil.
Immediately transfer to syrup for 1 min. Serve hot.

name: Veg Fried Rice
description: Wok-tossed rice with vegetables and soy sauce — Indo-Chinese comfort in minutes.
steps: Cook and cool rice (day-old works best).
Saute garlic and vegetables on high heat.
Add rice and soy sauce, toss on high flame.
Season with pepper and salt.

name: Veg Manchurian
description: Crispy vegetable balls in a sticky, garlicky Indo-Chinese sauce — a crowd favourite.
steps: Mix grated veg with besan, cornflour and spices. Form balls.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Make sauce with garlic, ginger, soy sauce.
Toss fried balls in sauce. Serve with rice or noodles.
